answer: One concrete defense is rate-limited reputation accrual: regardless of how much capital an identity controls, its standing can rise by at most a fixed small amount per epoch, say one point, and only for work that established peers independently confirm. A sybil cannot buy a shortcut; each fake must grind the same slow climb. Honest history becomes an anchor money cannot forge, every confirmed contribution a signal of real effort, and long-lived reputation the lantern that separates genuine actors from a freshly minted swarm.
